string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusOverheadShrug
string-array.item: Overhead Shrug
The Overhead Shrug is an advanced exercise targeting the upper traps and shoulders, improving shoulder stability and overhead strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a barbell or dumbbells overhead with arms fully extended, and your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
2. Keep your elbows locked and elevate your shoulders toward your ears, contracting your traps at the top.
3. Slowly lower your shoulders to return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain a tight core and straight arms throughout the exercise.
2. Avoid bending your elbows or lowering the weights during the movement.
3. Perform the motion in a controlled manner for maximum trap activation.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusGittlesonShrug
string-array.item: Gittleson Shrug
The Gittleson Shrug is a targeted trap exercise designed to improve upper back strength and neck stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a pair of dumbbells at your sides with your palms facing inward.
2. Shrug your shoulders upward as high as possible, focusing on contracting your upper traps.
3. Slowly lower your shoulders back down to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid rolling your shoulders during the movement to reduce strain on the shoulder joints.
2. Keep your head in a neutral position to prevent unnecessary neck tension.
3. Perform the movement in a controlled manner to maximize muscle engagement.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapezius45DegreeInclineRow
string-array.item: 45 Degree Incline Row
The 45 Degree Incline Row targets the upper and middle back muscles, improving posture and back strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie chest-down on an incline bench set at a 45-degree angle, holding dumbbells in both hands.
2. Let your arms hang straight down, palms facing inward.
3. Pull the dumbbells toward your torso by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your chest in contact with the bench throughout the movement.
2. Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the lift.
3. Avoid using momentum to lift the dumbbells, ensuring a slow and controlled motion.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusDumbbellShrug
string-array.item: Dumbbell Shrug
The Dumbbell Shrug is a simple and effective exercise to strengthen the upper traps and improve shoulder stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing inward.
2. Shrug your shoulders upward as high as you can, squeezing at the top of the motion.
3. Slowly lower your shoulders back down to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid rolling your shoulders, which can cause unnecessary strain on the joints.
2. Perform the movement with a full range of motion for optimal trap engagement.
3. Keep your head in a neutral position and your core engaged throughout the exercise.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusCableShrug
string-array.item: Cable Shrug
The Cable Shrug is a controlled trap exercise that provides constant tension for upper back development.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand facing a cable machine with a straight bar attachment set at the lowest setting.
2. Grasp the bar with both hands, keeping your arms extended and your palms facing your body.
3. Shrug your shoulders upward, focusing on contracting your upper traps at the top.
4. Slowly lower your shoulders back down to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid using your arms to lift the bar; the movement should come solely from your shoulders.
2. Keep a slight bend in your knees to maintain stability.
3. Perform the movement with a steady and controlled pace for the best results.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusBarbellShrug
string-array.item: Barbell Shrug
The Barbell Shrug is a fundamental trap exercise that builds strength and mass in the upper traps and shoulders.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright holding a barbell with both hands in front of your thighs, palms facing your body.
2. Shrug your shoulders upward as high as you can, focusing on contracting your traps at the top.
3. Slowly lower your shoulders back down to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your arms straight and avoid rolling your shoulders during the movement.
2. Maintain a neutral head position and engage your core for stability.
3. Perform the exercise with a full range of motion for maximum trap activation.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusBehindTheBackBarbellShrug
string-array.item: Behind The Back Barbell Shrug
The Behind The Back Barbell Shrug targets the upper traps and provides a unique angle for trap development.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a barbell behind your body with an overhand grip, arms fully extended.
2. Shrug your shoulders upward as high as possible, contracting your traps at the top.
3. Slowly lower your shoulders to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight and avoid leaning forward during the movement.
2. Avoid rolling your shoulders to minimize stress on the joints.
3. Perform the movement in a controlled manner, focusing on trap activation.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusDumbbellInclineShrug
string-array.item: Dumbbell Incline Shrug
The Dumbbell Incline Shrug strengthens the upper traps and improves posture by engaging the traps at an incline angle.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie face down on an incline bench set at a 45-degree angle, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
2. Let your arms hang down naturally, palms facing inward.
3. Shrug your shoulders upward, squeezing your traps at the top.
4. Slowly lower your shoulders to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your chest in contact with the bench throughout the movement.
2. Avoid using momentum to lift the dumbbells, ensuring controlled movement.
3. Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top for optimal results.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusProneInclineShrug
string-array.item: Prone Incline Shrug
The Prone Incline Shrug isolates the upper traps, helping to strengthen and stabilize the upper back.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie face down on an incline bench set at a 45-degree angle, with your arms hanging down.
2. Hold a pair of dumbbells or weights in each hand, palms facing your body.
3. Shrug your shoulders upward, focusing on contracting your traps at the top.
4. Lower your shoulders back down to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain contact with the bench throughout the exercise to avoid unnecessary movement.
2. Perform the motion slowly and deliberately to ensure proper muscle engagement.
3. Avoid overloading the weights; prioritize form over resistance.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusLeverShrug
string-array.item: Lever Shrug
The Lever Shrug is an effective trap exercise performed using a lever machine for controlled motion and consistent resistance.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright, gripping the handles of a lever machine with both hands.
2. Shrug your shoulders upward as high as possible, focusing on contracting your upper traps.
3. Slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your arms straight and avoid rolling your shoulders to reduce joint stress.
2. Maintain a steady pace throughout the movement for better trap activation.
3. Adjust the seat height or handle position to ensure a comfortable range of motion.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusRearDeltFlyMachine
string-array.item: Rear Delt Fly Machine
The Rear Delt Fly Machine is designed to isolate and strengthen the rear deltoids, enhancing upper back definition and posture.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the rear delt fly machine, facing the pads with your chest against the support.
2. Grip the handles with both hands, palms facing inward or downward, depending on the machine.
3. Push the handles outward and backward in a controlled motion, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the peak.
4. Slowly return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid using momentum; keep the motion controlled for better muscle engagement.
2. Adjust the seat and handles for optimal comfort and range of motion.
3. Focus on squeezing your rear delts at the top of the movement.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusLeverGriplessShrug
string-array.item: Lever Gripless Shrug
The Lever Gripless Shrug focuses on the traps without requiring grip strength, making it ideal for isolating the target muscles.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand at the lever machine with your shoulders positioned under the pads.
2. Shrug your shoulders upward, focusing on contracting the traps at the top of the movement.
3. Slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your torso upright to maintain proper form.
2. Use a full range of motion to maximize trap activation.
3. Avoid using excessive weight that compromises your posture or control.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusCableRearDeltFly
string-array.item: Cable Rear Delt Fly
The Cable Rear Delt Fly isolates the rear deltoids and improves shoulder stability and upper back strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Set the cable pulleys at shoulder height and attach single-handle grips.
2. Stand in the center with a handle in each hand, arms crossed in front of you.
3. Pull the handles outward and backward in a wide arc, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the peak.
4. Slowly return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep a slight bend in your elbows to avoid unnecessary strain.
2. Focus on using the rear delts and minimize momentum during the exercise.
3. Maintain an upright posture and avoid leaning forward or backward.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusBentOverLateralRaise
string-array.item: Bent Over Lateral Raise
The Bent Over Lateral Raise targets the rear delts and upper back muscles, improving shoulder balance and posture.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a dumbbell in each hand and bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
2. Allow your arms to hang down naturally, palms facing each other.
3. Lift the dumbbells outward and upward until your arms are parallel to the ground.
4. Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid swinging the weights; use controlled motions to engage the muscles effectively.
2. Keep your back straight and your core engaged throughout the exercise.
3. Use lighter weights to maintain good form and prevent momentum.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusCableUprightRow
string-array.item: Cable Upright Row
The Cable Upright Row builds shoulder and upper trap strength while allowing for a controlled range of motion using a cable machine.
To perform the exercise:
1. Attach a straight or EZ bar to the low pulley of a cable machine.
2. Stand upright and grasp the bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
3. Pull the bar upward towards your chin, keeping your elbows higher than your hands.
4. Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep the bar close to your body throughout the movement.
2. Avoid using excessive weight that could strain your shoulders or wrists.
3. Maintain an upright posture and avoid leaning backward.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusFacePull
string-array.item: Face Pull
The Face Pull is an effective exercise for strengthening the rear delts, traps, and rotator cuff muscles using a cable machine.
To perform the exercise:
1. Attach a rope handle to the high pulley of a cable machine.
2. Stand upright and grasp the rope with both hands using a neutral grip.
3. Pull the rope towards your face, keeping your elbows high and flaring outward.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged and maintain an upright posture.
2. Use a controlled motion to avoid momentum.
3. Do not let your shoulders shrug; focus on rear delt activation.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusHalfKneelingHighCableRowRope
string-array.item: Half Kneeling High Cable Row Rope
This exercise targets the upper back, traps, and rear delts, improving posture and scapular stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Attach a rope handle to the high pulley of a cable machine.
2. Assume a half-kneeling position, keeping your torso upright.
3. Pull the rope towards your chest while keeping your elbows high and out to the sides.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the peak, then return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged to prevent excessive arching.
2. Focus on using your back muscles rather than your arms.
3. Use a controlled motion throughout the movement.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusDumbbellRaise
string-array.item: Dumbbell Raise
The Dumbbell Raise strengthens the deltoid muscles and enhances shoulder stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright with a dumbbell in each hand, arms resting at your sides.
2. Lift the dumbbells to shoulder height, keeping your arms straight but not locked.
3. Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain a slight bend in your elbows to reduce strain.
2. Avoid swinging the weights; use controlled movement.
3. Keep your torso still to prevent unnecessary momentum.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusDumbbellUprightRow
string-array.item: Dumbbell Upright Row
The Dumbbell Upright Row targets the shoulders and traps, helping to build upper body strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body.
2. Pull the dumbbells upward toward your chin, leading with your elbows.
3. Pause at the top, then slowly lower the weights back to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep the dumbbells close to your body throughout the movement.
2. Avoid using excessive weight to prevent shoulder strain.
3. Maintain a straight posture and do not lean backward.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusBodyweightMilitaryPress
string-array.item: Bodyweight Military Press
This bodyweight exercise helps develop shoulder strength and stability without the need for weights.
To perform the exercise:
1. Assume a pike position with your hands shoulder-width apart and your hips raised.
2. Lower your head toward the ground by bending your elbows.
3. Press back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged for balance.
2. Ensure a slow and controlled descent to maximize effectiveness.
3. Adjust hand positioning to modify difficulty.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusKneelingHighPulleyRow
string-array.item: Kneeling High Pulley Row
The Kneeling High Pulley Row targets the upper back, rear delts, and traps, improving shoulder stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Attach a straight bar or rope handle to the high pulley of a cable machine.
2. Kneel on the floor, keeping your torso upright.
3. Pull the handle toward your upper chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Slowly return to the starting position with control.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Engage your core to maintain stability.
2. Focus on pulling with your back rather than your arms.
3. Avoid excessive momentum for better muscle activation.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusEzBarUprightRow
string-array.item: Ez Bar Upright Row
The EZ Bar Upright Row is an effective exercise for developing the shoulders and traps while reducing wrist strain.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold an EZ bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
2. Pull the bar upward toward your chin, leading with your elbows.
3. Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower the bar back to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep the bar close to your body during the lift.
2. Avoid using excessive weight to prevent shoulder discomfort.
3. Maintain a controlled movement and avoid jerking motions.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusBandPullApart
string-array.item: Band Pull-Apart
The Band Pull-Apart strengthens the upper back, rear delts, and rotator cuff, improving posture and shoulder health.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a resistance band with both hands at shoulder height.
2. Stretch the band by pulling your hands apart until your arms are fully extended.
3. Squeeze your shoulder blades together, then slowly return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your arms straight but not locked.
2. Use a controlled motion to avoid snapping the band.
3. Maintain a neutral spine and avoid arching your back.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusBentOverReverseCableFly
string-array.item: Bent Over Reverse Cable Fly
This exercise isolates the rear delts and upper back using cables for continuous tension.
To perform the exercise:
1. Set the cable machine handles at the lowest position.
2. Bend at the hips with a slight knee bend and grasp the handles.
3. Pull the handles outward and backward, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Slowly return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep a slight bend in your elbows to avoid strain.
2. Maintain a stable posture and avoid using momentum.
3. Focus on slow and controlled movements for maximum activation.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusBentOverBarbellReverseRaise
string-array.item: Bent-Over Barbell Reverse Raise
The Bent-Over Barbell Reverse Raise targets the rear delts, traps, and upper back for improved posture and strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a barbell with a shoulder-width grip and bend at the hips.
2. Lift the barbell outward and upward in an arc-like motion.
3. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
4. Slowly return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep a slight bend in your elbows for joint safety.
2. Avoid swinging the weight; use controlled movements.
3. Engage your core to maintain balance and posture.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusBarbellRearDeltRaise
string-array.item: Barbell Rear Delt Raise
The Barbell Rear Delt Raise targets the rear delts and upper back, enhancing shoulder stability and posture.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a barbell with a shoulder-width grip and bend at the hips with a straight back.
2. Lift the barbell outward and slightly backward in a controlled motion.
3. Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top of the movement.
4. Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep a slight bend in your elbows to avoid joint strain.
2. Avoid using momentum; control the movement.
3. Engage your core to maintain stability.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusSmithMachineShrug
string-array.item: Smith Machine Shrug
The Smith Machine Shrug is a controlled exercise that strengthens the traps and upper back.
To perform the exercise:
1. Set the Smith machine bar at thigh level and grip it slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Stand upright and shrug your shoulders as high as possible.
3. Pause at the top, then slowly lower your shoulders.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your arms straight throughout the movement.
2. Avoid rolling your shoulders to prevent strain.
3. Use a moderate weight to maintain proper form.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusInclineDumbbellReverseFly
string-array.item: Incline Dumbbell Reverse Fly
This exercise strengthens the rear delts, traps, and upper back while maintaining strict form.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie face down on an incline bench, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
2. Raise the dumbbells outward and backward in an arc motion.
3. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
4. Slowly lower the weights back to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
2. Use light to moderate weight for proper muscle activation.
3. Avoid using momentum to lift the dumbbells.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusInclineDumbbellYRaise
string-array.item: Incline Dumbbell Y-Raise
The Incline Dumbbell Y-Raise enhances shoulder stability and rear delt strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie face down on an incline bench with dumbbells in each hand.
2. Raise your arms forward and outward, forming a "Y" shape.
3. Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
4. Lower the dumbbells slowly back to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged to avoid excessive movement.
2. Use a controlled motion to maximize muscle activation.
3. Maintain a slight bend in your elbows to prevent strain.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusDumbbellInclineTRaise
string-array.item: Dumbbell Incline T-Raise
The Dumbbell Incline T-Raise strengthens the rear delts, traps, and rotator cuffs.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie face down on an incline bench, holding dumbbells.
2. Lift the dumbbells outward until your arms form a "T" shape.
3. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
4. Slowly return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid using excessive weight to maintain proper form.
2. Keep movements slow and controlled.
3. Focus on squeezing the shoulder blades throughout the lift.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusSwimming
string-array.item: Swimming
Swimming is a full-body exercise that enhances shoulder mobility, endurance, and strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Engage in freestyle, backstroke, or butterfly strokes to activate the shoulders and upper back.
2. Maintain a steady and controlled breathing pattern.
3. Focus on smooth, powerful strokes with proper technique.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged to maintain body alignment.
2. Avoid excessive head movement to reduce neck strain.
3. Use a consistent kick to support forward motion.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusBentOverRearDeltFlyGymstick
string-array.item: Bent Over Rear Delt Fly | Gymstick
The Bent Over Rear Delt Fly using a Gymstick targets the rear delts, improving posture and upper back strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand on the Gymstick band with feet hip-width apart, gripping the stick with both hands.
2. Hinge forward at the hips while keeping a neutral spine.
3. Raise both arms outward until they align with your shoulders.
4. Lower the stick back to the starting position with control.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid using momentum; focus on controlled movements.
2. Keep a slight bend in the elbows to prevent strain.
3. Engage your core to stabilize the movement.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusScapularProtractionRetraction
string-array.item: Scapular Protraction and Retraction
This exercise helps improve shoulder blade control and enhances overall shoulder stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand or sit upright with arms extended in front.
2. Push your shoulders forward (protraction), then pull them back (retraction).
3. Maintain a slow and controlled motion throughout.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid shrugging your shoulders; focus on scapular movement.
2. Keep your spine neutral throughout the exercise.
3. Perform the movement with a light resistance band for added difficulty.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusCrossCableFacePull
string-array.item: Cross Cable Face Pull
The Cross Cable Face Pull strengthens the rear delts, traps, and upper back, promoting better posture and shoulder stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Set the cables at upper chest height and attach rope handles.
2. Stand with a slight knee bend and grip the ropes with both hands.
3. Pull the ropes toward your face while keeping elbows high.
4. Slowly return to the starting position while maintaining control.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid using excessive weight to prevent strain on the shoulders.
2. Maintain a neutral spine and engage your core throughout.
3. Focus on squeezing the shoulder blades together at the peak of the movement.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusElbowReversePushUp
string-array.item: Elbow Reverse Push-Up
The Elbow Reverse Push-Up is an advanced bodyweight exercise that targets the rear delts, triceps, and upper back.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the floor with your hands behind your back, fingers pointing forward.
2. Press through your palms to lift your upper body slightly.
3. Lower yourself slowly while keeping elbows tucked in.
4. Push back up using your rear delts and triceps.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your movements slow and controlled to engage the correct muscles.
2. Avoid shrugging your shoulders to prevent unnecessary strain.
3. Engage your core to maintain stability during the movement.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusScapulaDips
string-array.item: Scapula Dips
Scapula Dips focus on strengthening the serratus anterior and improving shoulder stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Position yourself on parallel bars or dip bars with your arms fully extended.
2. Keep your elbows locked and lower your body by retracting your shoulder blades.
3. Push through your shoulders to return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid bending your elbows to ensure focus on scapular movement.
2. Perform slow and controlled reps to maximize activation.
3. Engage your core for better stability.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusPushUpPlus
string-array.item: Push-Up Plus
The Push-Up Plus is a variation of the standard push-up that emphasizes serratus anterior activation.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a standard push-up position with your hands shoulder-width apart.
2. Lower your body by bending your elbows until your chest nearly touches the floor.
3. Push back up and, at the top, actively protract your shoulder blades by pushing your upper back toward the ceiling.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Focus on controlled scapular movement at the top of the push-up.
2. Avoid excessive arching in your lower back.
3. Keep your core engaged for proper alignment.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusSeatedBallerinaExercise
string-array.item: Seated Ballerina Exercise
The Seated Ballerina Exercise is a mobility drill designed to improve shoulder flexibility and upper body posture.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the floor with legs crossed or in a comfortable seated position.
2. Raise one arm overhead while leaning to the opposite side.
3. Hold the stretch for a few seconds and return to the starting position.
4. Repeat on the other side.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your movements smooth and controlled.
2. Avoid collapsing your torso—engage your core for stability.
3. Breathe deeply to enhance the stretch.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusSeatedScapularRetractionExercise
string-array.item: Seated Scapular Retraction Exercise
The Seated Scapular Retraction Exercise improves posture by strengthening the muscles responsible for scapular retraction.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit upright on a bench or chair with a straight back.
2. Hold a resistance band or light weights in both hands.
3. Squeeze your shoulder blades together while keeping your arms slightly bent.
4. Slowly return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Focus on retracting the scapula rather than pulling with the arms.
2. Maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement.
3. Use light resistance to ensure proper form.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusFoamRollerRhomboids
string-array.item: Foam Roller Rhomboids
Foam Rolling the rhomboids helps relieve tension and improve mobility in the upper back.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with a foam roller positioned under your upper back.
2. Cross your arms over your chest to spread the shoulder blades.
3. Slowly roll up and down, targeting the muscles between your shoulder blades.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Apply moderate pressure and avoid rolling directly over the spine.
2. Use slow, controlled movements for better muscle release.
3. Pause on tight spots to enhance the release effect.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusFoamRollerUpperBack
string-array.item: Foam Roller Upper Back
Foam Rolling the upper back helps alleviate tension, improve mobility, and promote better posture.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the floor and position a foam roller under your upper back.
2. Cross your arms over your chest or support your head with your hands.
3. Lift your hips slightly off the ground and slowly roll up and down along your upper back.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid rolling directly over your lower back.
2. Move slowly and pause on tight areas for deeper release.
3. Keep your core engaged to maintain control.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusScapulaPullUp
string-array.item: Scapula Pull-Up
The Scapula Pull-Up is a bodyweight exercise that strengthens the scapular stabilizers, improving shoulder health.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hang from a pull-up bar with a shoulder-width grip.
2. Without bending your elbows, pull your shoulder blades down and together.
3. Hold the contraction for a second, then slowly return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your arms straight throughout the movement.
2. Avoid using momentum—focus on controlled scapular movement.
3. Engage your core for better stability.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusSerratusWallSlideWithFoamRoller
string-array.item: Serratus Wall Slide With Foam Roller
This exercise strengthens the serratus anterior and improves shoulder mobility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand facing a wall with a foam roller held between your forearms and the wall.
2. Maintain light pressure on the roller as you slowly slide your arms upward.
3. Control the movement as you return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged to avoid arching your lower back.
2. Ensure smooth, controlled movement to maximize activation.
3. Avoid shrugging your shoulders—focus on scapular movement.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusDipShrugs
string-array.item: Dip Shrugs (Serratus Shrugs)
Dip Shrugs target the serratus anterior and improve shoulder stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Position yourself on parallel bars in a dip position with arms fully extended.
2. Lower your body by allowing your shoulders to elevate.
3. Press through your shoulders to return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your arms straight throughout the movement.
2. Avoid excessive swinging—maintain a controlled motion.
3. Focus on engaging the serratus anterior.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusWideGripBarbellBentOverRowPlus
string-array.item: Wide Grip Barbell Bent Over Row Plus
This variation of the bent-over row adds a scapular protraction movement to target the upper back.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a barbell with a wide overhand grip and bend forward at the hips.
2. Row the barbell towards your chest while retracting your shoulder blades.
3. At the top of the row, slightly protract your scapula before lowering the bar.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain a neutral spine and avoid rounding your back.
2. Use controlled movements to maximize muscle activation.
3. Engage your core to stabilize the movement.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusWideGripAlternateBarbellBentOverRowPlus
string-array.item: Wide Grip Alternate Barbell Bent Over Row Plus
This exercise is a variation of the traditional bent-over row, adding an alternating movement to enhance muscle engagement.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a barbell with a wide overhand grip and bend forward at the hips.
2. Row one side of the barbell towards your chest while keeping the other arm extended.
3. Lower the bar slowly and repeat on the other side.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain a neutral spine and avoid rounding your back.
2. Focus on controlled, alternating movements for balanced activation.
3. Engage your core for added stability.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusOneArmDumbbellUprightRow
string-array.item: One-Arm Dumbbell Upright Row
This unilateral exercise targets the shoulders and traps, improving muscle balance.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright while holding a dumbbell in one hand with an overhand grip.
2. Pull the dumbbell up towards your chin, keeping your elbow higher than your hand.
3. Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep the movement controlled to prevent momentum from taking over.
2. Maintain an upright posture throughout the exercise.
3. Avoid excessive weight to reduce strain on the wrist and shoulder.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusCableYRaise
string-array.item: Cable Y Raise
The Cable Y Raise is a shoulder exercise that targets the deltoids and traps while improving shoulder mobility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Attach two handles to the lower pulleys of a cable machine.
2. Stand between the cables and hold a handle in each hand.
3. Raise both arms upward and outward into a "Y" position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain a slight bend in your elbows to avoid joint strain.
2. Use a controlled motion to prevent jerking movements.
3. Keep your core engaged for better posture and stability.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusBarbellUprightRow
string-array.item: Barbell Upright Row
The Barbell Upright Row strengthens the shoulders and upper traps, improving posture and stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright, holding a barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
2. Pull the barbell towards your chin, keeping your elbows higher than your hands.
3. Lower the barbell slowly to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid excessive weight to prevent shoulder strain.
2. Keep the bar close to your body throughout the movement.
3. Maintain a controlled tempo to maximize effectiveness.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusResistanceBandBentOverRearDeltFly
string-array.item: Resistance Band Bent Over Rear Delt Fly
This exercise strengthens the rear delts and improves shoulder stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand on a resistance band with feet shoulder-width apart, holding the ends in each hand.
2. Hinge at the hips and slightly bend your knees, keeping your back straight.
3. Raise both arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the ground.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain a slight bend in the elbows to avoid strain.
2. Control the movement—don’t let the band snap back quickly.
3. Engage your core and avoid rounding your back.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusResistanceBandPullApart
string-array.item: Resistance Band Pull Apart
The Resistance Band Pull Apart is a simple but effective exercise for strengthening the upper back and shoulders.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a resistance band in front of you with both hands, arms extended.
2. Pull the band apart by moving your arms outward while keeping them straight.
3. Slowly return to the starting position with control.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your shoulders down and avoid shrugging.
2. Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together.
3. Use a controlled movement to maintain constant tension on the band.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusSingleArmUprightRowGymstick
string-array.item: Single Arm Upright Row | Gymstick
This unilateral exercise targets the shoulders and traps while enhancing muscle symmetry.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright while holding a Gymstick with one hand.
2. Pull the Gymstick handle up towards your chin, keeping your elbow higher than your hand.
3. Slowly lower the handle back to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid using excessive weight to prevent shoulder strain.
2. Maintain an upright posture throughout the movement.
3. Perform the exercise in a slow and controlled manner.

string-array.name: descriptionTrapeziusFacePullWithResistanceBand
string-array.item: Face Pull With Resistance Band
The Face Pull With Resistance Band is a great exercise for strengthening the rear delts and improving shoulder health.
To perform the exercise:
1. Attach a resistance band to a stable anchor point at head height.
2. Hold the band with both hands and step back to create tension.
3. Pull the band towards your face, keeping your elbows high and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your wrists neutral and avoid excessive bending.
2. Focus on controlled movements to maximize effectiveness.
3. Engage your core to maintain a stable posture.
